findings.title: System-gesture preference probes never start their prepared ShellRunner tasks
guarantees: System-owned macOS gesture slots are withheld to prevent native and Ergopti double actions.
An accepted asynchronous preference refresh eventually observes a native terminal or reports failure.

reproduction.observed: Actual ShellRunner constructs4 native task doubles; starts0, callback0; repeated recheck joins pending probe, swipe_3_left stays free. Starting the exact4 retained handles and completing enabled preference reads changes it to taken.
reproduction.boundaries: Real conflict module and real ShellRunner lifecycle over hs.task native doubles; no real commands, macOS settings or native actions.

findings.root_cause: macos/modules/gestures/conflicts.lua:259-296 calls ShellRunner.spawn and retains/checks handles but never calls handle.start. Real shell_runner.lua:784 prepares, :793 exposes start, :831 returns without starting. snapshot_ready never changes, so conflict slots initially return free.
findings.silent_failure: Refresh returns true without a start error; pending probe never drains and native conflict warning/disable policy has no actual settings snapshot.
findings.regression_test: Use real ShellRunner with recording native task construction/start/terminal; require four starts and terminal/failure settlement; repeat refresh and settings changes, exact shutdown, and fail-closed slot admission before first snapshot. Existing spawn doubles must model prepared/start lifecycle.

findings.title: Tap commit dispatch bypasses the macOS system-gesture conflict gate
guarantees: A macOS-owned tap_3 slot does not execute an Ergopti action while native Look up owns it.
Tap and swipe dispatch apply the same native-system slot admission.

reproduction.observed: Real engine with system_held always true dispatches lookup on stationary3-contact tap/lift and never queries predicate. Horizontal swipe control queries same predicate and dispatches nothing.
reproduction.boundaries: Real gesture engine over native touch/clock/eventtap doubles; action recorders only, no real lookup or output.

findings.root_cause: engine.lua:700-716 calls dispatchAction directly in tap branch; triggerAction:451-459 alone applies state.system_held. multiFingerAllowed:300 checks physical recognition policy, not native ownership. conflicts.lua:120-127 explicitly declares tap_3 blocking.
findings.silent_failure: Tap logs TAP FIRE with no conflict rejection even when system-held state is true; fixes to preference probing do not fix this independent dispatch omission.
findings.regression_test: Replay real tap commit for taken/unverified/free tap_3 state; assert no dispatch while held and one single-shot dispatch when free, alongside existing swipe control, AI and pause gates.
